items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: One of the earliest guys that wrote on jazz in New Orleans, of course, was Preston Jackson.

ctx.x: As a matter of fact, Leroy Jones wrote an article, wrote a chapter in his book, Blues People, talking about jazz. He called it Jazz and the White Critics. He wanted to point out the fact that jazz, as a black art, not exclusively, but in large part in some respects. It's always been brought to the attention by white critics.
One of the earliest guys that wrote on jazz in New Orleans, of course, was Preston Jackson. That's right.
I was thinking about that, too.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: He was just an enthusiast, jazz enthusiast.

ctx.x: When they were giving those slow drag dances in the 1950s. Bill Russell was promoting dances in England. It was Bill who was doing it?

Yeah, Bill Russell. He did it for about six weeks or something like that. He wasn't trying to make money, he was just trying to, if he could get his money back. He was just an enthusiast, jazz enthusiast. But the crowds varied quite a bit.
You weren't doing much in the 50s at all.
